Using synthetic data based on two example general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) model images of M87, we performed case studies to assess the image quality that can be obtained with the current and future EHT array for different weather conditions.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00841.V.
the visibilities are split into 64 channels spanning a bandwidth of 2 GHz centred at 228 GHz, which is the central EHT observation frequency.
The EHT2017 schedule for 11 April was adopted.
Our primary array consists of the 2017 EHT stations, excluding the SPT station for which M87 is always below the horizon.
We base our scientific studies primarily on a GRMHD simulation of the jet launching region of M87 from (cite: Davelaar2019).
we use `SYMBA` to simulate observations of GRMHD model images by (cite: Dexter2012) and (cite: Moscibrodzka2016).
we used the median values measured during the EHT2017 campaign (5-11 April) at the individual primary sites, logged by the VLBI monitor (cite: eht-paperII).
We use a simple 4 Jy point source model to study signal corruption and calibration effects.
the synthetic data are passed through the `rPICARD` calibration pipeline (cite: Janssen2019).
The visibility phases are then self-calibrated and used for imaging as well, while maintaining the closure quantity fits.
The images are reconstructed with a regularized maximum likelihood (RML) method using the `eht-imaging` software.
The fiducial parameters and regularizers (Maximum Entropy, Total Variation, and Total Squared Variation) obtained from an extensive parameter survey by (cite: eht-paperIV) are adopted.
We briefly describe the added tropospheric and instrumental corruptions below, referring to (cite: Blecher2017) and (cite: Natarajan2019) for more details.
`MeqSilhouette` predicts visibilities directly from the Fourier Transform of an input sky model.
the smallest timescale which yields fringe detections with S/N\>5.5 on all baselines for which the source can be detected, is chosen

We then calibrate the raw data using the new `CASA` (cite: McMullin2007) VLBI data calibration pipeline `rPICARD`
a ‘network calibration’ (cite: Fish2011; Johnson2015; Blackburn2019; eht-paperIII) is performed with the `eht-imaging` software.

we then perform radiative transfer at 225 GHz with the `am` atmospheric model software (cite: Paine2019)
This GRMHD simulation is performed with the code `BHAC` (cite: Porth2017)
The GRMHD simulation is post-processed with the general relativistic ray tracing code `RAPTOR` (cite: bronzwaer2018).

In this paper, we present the SYnthetic Measurement creator for long Baseline Arrays (`SYMBA`) – a new synthetic VLBI data generation and calibration pipeline.
